verified.exploit_entry_point: The built daemon binary, started on loopback ports by each test with a fresh database: the tests open the live event stream with a foreign/host-suffix/encoded-path request, and POST to the state-changing API paths (ordinary and dispatch-equivalent encoded spellings) with a foreign Origin, then read the mailbox totals and a local SMTP sink for side effects. Because the tests drive the real process over its public HTTP surface, a fix at any layer (route wiring, shared middleware, handlers, listener wiring) is exercised.
sites: server/websockets/client.go:37-38 (CheckOrigin unconditionally true at the pin)
server/server.go:199 (the event-stream route is registered outside middleWareFunc)
server/server.go:287,291 (path-scoped policy decides on r.RequestURI, the raw target)
server/server.go:267-325 (middleWareFunc sets CORS headers but never decides on Origin)
server/apiv1/send.go:45-49 (decodes the body with no Origin or content-type decision)
routes: T1: live event stream handshake from a foreign origin, and with cached basic credentials
T2: the same handshake once the fix is placed only in the shared middleware (the route bypasses it)
T3: a dispatch-equivalent encoded request target on the state-changing route
T6: cross-origin simple POST to the send and release routes
verified.services: none: loopback HTTP/SMTP only; no external network
verified.project_tests_run: go test ./server -count=1 at the pinned commit, and on the oracle/alt/hardening and every check patch

traps.shape: the live event stream accepts a handshake from any origin; a browser attaches its cached basic credentials to the cross-origin handshake, so the stream's new-message summaries reach the page. Coupled must-keep-working: the same-origin UI, clients that send no origin, and a non-root webroot
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the line is commented as deliberately allowing multi-domain use, the socket only pushes notifications, and ServeWs performs its own basic-auth check
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-524m-q5m7-79mm); the unconditional CheckOrigin is the original Gorilla-derived handler

traps.shape: the event-stream route is registered outside the shared request middleware, so an admission decision added to that middleware never runs for the socket; the handler looks self-contained because it repeats the basic-auth check
traps.reason_to_dismiss: every other UI/API route is wrapped in the shared middleware, but this one is not; ServeWs performs its own basic-auth check, so the handler reads as deliberately self-contained
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the route registration predates both advisories

traps.shape: a path-keyed admission decision is made from the raw request target instead of the path the router dispatched: a percent-encoded spelling still reaches the handler, but a lexical prefix test on the raw target does not match, so the decision is skipped. Coupled must-keep-working: the configured-origin CORS grant and the credential-less preflight on the same paths
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the existing path-scoped block reads the raw request target and looks like the right template; on its own it only adds a response header, so a raw/decoded mismatch fails closed and appears harmless
traps.realistic_because: published second fix (GHSA-8r62-w5wh-fc5m) changes exactly this decision; the pinned code still reads r.RequestURI

traps.shape: state-changing API requests have no origin decision at all: a browser issues a cross-origin simple POST without a preflight, and the handlers ignore both Origin and content type. The release route is a second sink family behind the same missing decision
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the API is unauthenticated by default and exists to be driven by local scripts and CI; the response-header CORS policy is assumed to cover cross-origin use, and release additionally needs relay configuration
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: neither published fix commit for these advisories touches the state-changing routes

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a panic in these handlers aborts the request with a 500 and the same side-effect assertion still fails, so it cannot act as a clean client-error refusal
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: this protection is a browser-origin boundary over the whole mailbox, not a per-object authorization decision
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles or peers exist on this surface; miss_concept_ws.patch and miss_concept_post.patch separate the read channel from the write channel
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: an unparsable, empty or duplicated Origin is refused closed, so no spelling makes the guard see nothing
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no credential or authority lookup participates in this decision

A.summary: Cross-site WebSocket hijacking: the event stream accepted a handshake from any origin

B.summary: Origin check bypass via a percent-encoded request target (incomplete earlier protection)
